## Historical audit: S0095

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/replay_s1_r1/M_descendant/C1/replay_selection/commons_29206714/trajectory.jsonl`. Only chunk 2 of 3 is visible; the referenced images themselves are not available to this audit.

| Evidence | Observation and limits |
|---|---|
| Student `model_request`, line 15, chars [0,187917) | The assigned goal was an editable reconstruction of one indoor RGB photograph, with separate meshes and a matching camera. The student's scene interpretation included a dresser, open doors, crockery, fireplace, yarn swift and foreground spinning wheel. These labels and anchor estimates are the student's interpretation, not independent identification of the photograph. |
| Student programs and reported results embedded in line 15 | The initial build specified multiple assets and components, colored finishes, procedural wood grain, a camera and two area lights. Doors had hinge-pivot rotations; the wheel had rims, spokes, hub and supports. Ownership and coordinates show intended assembly, not verified physical connection, contact or pose. Steps 1 and 2 were reported `ok: true`, with rendered-image paths. |
| Student revision embedded in line 15 | After step 1, the student reported a small crown, broad wheel and mantel overlap. The revision increased lens 52 to 64, raised the camera, moved the fireplace and wheel, changed wheel orientation and shortened swift rods. These simultaneous changes make individual causal effects uncertain. |
| Student `model_response`, line 17, chars [0,12051); `execute`, line 18, chars [0,12736) | The student claimed step 2's shelf/crown slopes disagreed and hypothesized the camera was on the wrong side; crown framing was said to be close and the wheel top too low. Step 3 moved the camera across the scene, preserved lens 64, changed wheel-plane angle and moved the wheel owner upward and sideways. This is an executed revision, not proof that the diagnosis was correct or that the wheel remains supported. |
| `execution_result`, line 19, chars [0,70092); `select`, lines 20–21, chars [0,59) each | Step 3 reported `ok: true`, completed a 16-sample render and saved an image and blend file. Step 3 was selected twice. This establishes formal execution success and selection, **not visual or geometric correctness**. No subsequent visual assessment is visible here. |
| Student `codex_session`, line 16, chars [0,3914) | The session listed the reference and two renders as input images, completed with zero tool calls, and ran with shell, browser and independent image-viewing tools disabled. The visible exploration was iterative program-and-runner revision, not autonomous external exploration. |

**Teacher input and outcome.** No teacher message, diagnosis or proposed update is visible in this chunk; teacher availability or adoption cannot be established. The runner's review instructions and success reports are not teacher feedback. The observed outcome is successful execution of three builds and selection of step 3; overall reconstruction quality and any final student judgment remain unknown, rather than demonstrably correct or an algorithm failure.

**Lessons and uncertainty.** Transferably, rendered output and grouped parts do not by themselves validate support, connectivity or reference fidelity; changing camera and object pose together also confounds diagnosis. Task-specific unresolved hypotheses are whether the camera-side reversal corrected slopes and door widths, whether the raised wheel matches the silhouette without floating, and whether fireplace occlusion, materials, textures and lighting match the photograph. No independent image, contact, collision or lighting verification is present in the visible evidence.
